#4134. Talking Point: What Are You Playing This Weekend? (7th November)

HYAAH, HUHH, HUP, HYAAH *coughing and splutting* Sorry about that, everyone. Welcome to another edition of What Are You Playing!

Just in case you somehow missed it, it was Zelda week this week as Ocarina of Time finally landed on Switch 2! The ensuing Ask the Developer interviews revealed the game's dev team, Aonuma's reasons for returning to it, Water Temple tweaks and more. There was also a wild midnight launch event in London, Metascore madness, new gameplay footage and more. In short, a lot of Zelda.

That's not all, though. Nintendo's latest financial report gave us updated Switch 2 sales figures, Pokémon Pokopia's next DLC wave got a release date, 'The Elder Scrolls 6' title was finally revealed, and The Pokémon Company continued its mysterious countdown.

Well hey, all that news means it must have been quiet in review land, right? Wrong! We shared our thoughts on Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered (7/10), Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy: Encore Edition (8/10), Stellar Blade: Complete Edition (7/10), Zero Parades: Director's Cut (8/10), and a little game called Ocarina of Time (9/10).

Phew. We can take a pretty good guess at what most of us will be playing this weekend, but let's have a look, just in case.

Guide Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Walkthrough (Switch 2 Remake): Guide To The Main Quest, Side Quests & Collectables

Feature "I Will Have Been Here For 30 Hours" - London's Midnight Zelda Launch Was Wild

My GOTY backlog grows by the day, with Pragmata, The Séance of Blake Manor, Well Dweller and more all sitting there waiting to be played. But who am I kidding? I didn't attend that midnight launch for nothing.

There's a part of me that wants to speed through the remake to see as many of the changes as possible before the year is up. There's another part that wants nothing more than to take my time with it and play nothing else ever again. Decisions, decisions, eh?

Look, obviously, I’ve got the cart. However, at the time of writing, it’s still sealed for a couple of reasons: 1) I was fortunate enough to play two hours pre-release, so I already know how good it looks and feels and I’m prolonging the excitement; and 2) we’re in the autumn section of Click Clock Wood in a Banjo playthrough and, being so close to the final quiz/battle with Grunty, I want to cap that off before diving into Hyrule with the kids.

GOTY is also approaching and I’m catching up with Requiem and Mixtape, and there’s a dozen other things on the backburner. How long can I resist the call of Kokiri Forest?

*rips the plastic off with teeth Sunday morning and spends all day playing in pyjamas

Hmmmm… I wonder what I’ll be playing this weekend? Surely it couldn’t be Ocarina of Time? Well, yes it will be. I still have some collectables to grab and medals I want to collect in the Zelda Notes app. Once I’ve made more progress in that, I am so tempted to return to my old OoT saves from the GameCube and 3DS games or even dabble with Majora’s Mask!

After going to the midnight launch in London, I left so inspired after chatting with fellow Hylians and like-minded superfans. Either way, the Zelda bug has taken a big ol’ chomp into me.

I will still be unlocking teams, skills and players in Tape to Tape this weekend. I also plan to start Eve’s epic journey in Stellar Blade Complete Edition. Being a huge fan of the series, it is quite unfortunate I failed to notice the release of Earth Defense Force 5 on Switch 2, but thankfully, NL readers recommendations saved the day, and I am once again quite hooked on blasting giant ants and spiders (I haven’t even unlocked any mechs yet!). Looking forward to E.D.F. 6 next year.

My game of the Week is NOT The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Yes, I too will be enjoying this quality remake while fondly remembering how simpler life was 28 years ago, but having one of my favourite GameCube games re-released with a brand new Unreal Engine 5 coat of paint is proving far too enticing. Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is my game of the week, and since there was also a surprise Switch 1 release, everyone should be able to (re)discover the joys of smashing a building into King Ghidorah (and do remember to ask the faeries for Mothra’s help, even if that sounds primitive and unscientific).

I’ve played a hell of a lot of Ocarina of Time recently, so I’m actually keen to play literally anything else. I’ve got my eye on Queen’s Domain: I’ve heard great things about it, and the visual style really speaks to me.

I also recently picked up Alone in the Dark via the PS5’s Black Friday sale, so I’d like to give that a go at some point. Some of the more middling reviews put me off in 2024, but with the cheeky discount, it’s about time I dive in. After jogging around Hyrule for so long, I’m ready for some comforting survival horror.

Those are our plans, but what about yours? Let us know what you'll be slapping in your Switch (2) in the poll below.

Jim came to Nintendo Life in 2022 and, despite his insistence that The Minish Cap is the best Zelda game and his unwavering love for the Star Wars prequels (yes, really), he has continued to write news and features on the site ever since.

I am COMPLETELY absorbed by World of Warcraft Forever. I doubt that I will play anything in the coming months ... sorry Zelda.

I finished The Lives Of The Necromancers by William Godwin (good, but hard going!), and am now reading The First Ghosts by Irving Finkel, a study of how ghosts were viewed in Mesopotamian culture.

ZOOT - Yeah, that's how I refer to it. 😆 It was hard to ignore this one. Not sure how I feel about it so far, so I won't comment just yet.

Banjo Kazooie (Evercade) - I have really been enjoying this! It's certainly a game which stands the test of time, and the improvements are good. Shame that you can't save within worlds without being kicked back to the hub, an improvement that I was really hoping for (they did that for ZOOT!), but it's still a beguiling game. Oh, and, for those interested... the Evercade Nexus is fantastic so far. A solid upgrade.

Have a lovely weekend, guys, and please take great care of yourselves out there.

Tonight I'm not seeing my friends so I'll just continue with my schedule:

Managed to finish Dave the Diver (which was excellent!) with a few days to spare, so naturally I booked yesterday off work to fully immerse myself in Ocarina of Time.

Sadly, my daughter had other plans. Her first day of nursery coincided perfectly with her catching hand, foot and mouth. Talk about timing! 😂

Still, I’ve managed to squeeze in enough time to conquer the first dungeon, do a spot of grave digging and get involved in some questionable mask salesman activities in Kakariko Village.

Honestly, I’m having an absolute blast. There’s something so magical about being back in Hyrule, and I’m trying to savour every minute of it.

Hope you’re all having a cracking weekend of gaming! 🎮

Something cool that I noticed is that the controller vibrates when playing the ocarina. The low D is a D, the F is an F, but the A sounds like another D on the controller, and the B sounds like an E and the high D sounds like a G. I guess it can't go very high, as it sounds like it struggles when I try to play anything higher than the high D (controller G). Strangely, it sounds like a B when I hold down on the stick and Z on the low D, but trying it on the A (controller D) sounds like it's partway between C and C#. Because only the top three notes are different, songs like Zelda's Lullaby and Epona's Song sound similar—just in a different key—from the controller, but songs that also use the lower two notes sound very strange, like Saria's Song being F D E. I can't use a tuner as it's too quiet so I might be completely wrong about this, haha... I'm kidding; my ears aren't that bad, I think...

I've done a massive clean up of my storage over the last few months, and I've been hoarding most Pokémon that meet the XL transfer threshold once that bonus returns (whenever that may be, oh, please, oh, please, oh, please!!!). I've got the current max storage of 13,000, and despite my vigorous spring cleaning, I'm relying on the bonus returning soon (it didn't return for Halloween this year ) so I can clear out close to (if not exceeding) 6,000 Pokémon, which will yield 18,000 XL candies, and I'll also get about half of my storage back... win-win! ^-^

If the XL transfer bonus returns, I'll also go through my excess shinies and delete some that meet the XL transfer threshold (basically, anything that normally requires at least 4 candies and 3,000 Stardust to power up) as I have yet to transfer any shiny that I've caught since I've been playing regularly in early 2024 (though I have sent a bunch to Home, but I'm limited to sending only 5-6 per week).

Blitzed through my first playthrough of the Ocarina of Time remake. Only thing I didn´t do was get all the golden skulltullas. Loved it, definitely playing it again in a year or so. Fingers crossed three times over that a Majoras Mask remake is coming in 2-3 years.

The social calendar is a bit busy for the rest of the weekend, so I suppose the few hours I get are gonna be spent continuing my replay of God of War Ragnarok. I wanted to refresh before Laufey comes out next year.

It should come as no surprise, but I will be playing Ocarina of Time, of course. Other games I am currently playing:

I must say it is very, very intriguing and well designed machine. I love the switch 2!

Dusk and FF IV are my options this weekend. Maybe I'll add some playtime on MH Rise and try another weapon on the busiest multiplayer hours

I'm playing this hidden gem I found that everyone should check out. It only came out on Thursday and my physical copy even had this special foil treatment on the cover. It's called The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. I highly recommend.

Also Minishoot Adventures as my physical finally came. Also brilliant

Rather than pay more than I’ve ever paid for a triple dip in The Water Temple, I picked up Queen’s Domain.

Up to now (2 of 3 blue balls flung into a lizards gaping mouth), this is my runaway GOTY. Honestly, if you can dance to it’s very particular tune it is just a sublime experience. Not a single clump of modern day fluff, immaculate world building that is somehow both reverent of the source material and quite unique. Genuinely superb level design so far too, honestly don’t know how such a tiny team can manage it. Even the slightly wonky arrangements of the music and sound design beautifully keep it’s feet in perhaps my favourite console generation.

An absolute triumph in every respect. Pulled me from the brink of becoming a jaded cynic. 11/10

I’m playing wishing I bought Ocarina of Time, but I’ve spent my whole budget in gaming, so Control Resonant maybe? I’m not really liking it though, which is a bummer as a longtime Remedy fan.

I’m starting to miss physical games because I wish I could sell some of my games I didn’t like to buy OoT, which I know I would.

Since my new Switch 2 arrived yesterday there is a lot to catch up on, the Ocarina of Time Remake, which has been the decisive reason for me to finally deep-dive into the Nintendo universe again after ages on other systems, arrived besides Metroid Prime Remastered, Metroid Prime 4 Beyond, Breath of the Wild & Tears of the Kingdom and I can't even remember the last time I've been this excited to greet the postman ringing my doorbell!

After years of digital "ownership" playing on PS5 trying to enjoy modern AAA slop, Nintendo & the Switch 2 finally gave me the good reason & feeling again to purchase physical media & enjoy meaningful videogame craftsmanship with titles I haven't seen & experienced for a very long time when I last booted my GameCube back in the days.

I'm quite sure I'll be in for a treat with the new system & all these games and I hope you all will have a great & healthy weekend.

Hello again, y'all! This weekend I'm playing:

Switch 2: Neptunia x Senran Kagura Ninja Wars: It's really good so far, think Hyrule Warriors but with way fewer monsters on the map, and more linear stages so far. I'm already on chapter 3.

Darkwood - almost gave up a couple of time but sticking with it and enjoying it when I don’t die 3 times in a row! About to go into the second half I think - I seem to be taking a long time compared to the average…

Not got Ocarina remake but maybe I’ll ask for it for Xmas. I don’t tend to replay games multiple times but I do have very fond memories of playing this when it came out so feels like I really should.

Also tempted to get ff7 rebirth in the sale. So cheap!

I’ve finished my playthrough of Metroid Prime 4 (really enjoyed it!). Still playing through Fire Emblem Echoes (really love it, might be my favoriet FE game so far!) and that has kept me tickled for Fortune’s Weave, which I got yesterday. Gonne start FW tonight and expect to be playing that for the coming 2 or 3 months…

Zelda! Zelda! Zelda! (75% of my game time)25%: My daily dose of Animal Crossing (20 Minutes), Splatoon Raiders (20 Minutes), Pokopia (20 Minutes), Pokémon Z-A (30 Minutes) and Kirby Raiders (30 Minutes)

Hey, its weekend, i can play as much as i want

I started it yesterday and it's glorious. Stendhal effect at its best.

Just Splatoon 3 and Tears of the Kingdom for me. Waiting on stores around me to restock Ocarina of Time, so I can get that.

Continuing with Shadow of the Tomb Raider, interestingly I've already reached beyond where I got in my Xbox save file years ago.

Well, the wife and I flew into Chicago yesterday for the Bears game this Sunday. Already had some good deep dish pizza & beer and grabbed some of those expresso martinis at the Starbucks Reserve here. Place is huge.

Today we're doing a tour of Wrigley Field and hitting up Wrigleyville afterwards for a Chicago dog and my wife says I must have a "Chicago Handshake". Okie dokie I guess. Fancy dinner somewhere tonight and then the Bears game Sunday.

Anyways, of course I brought my Switch 2 so I put more hours into Everspace 2 on the plane. I was able to just about wrap up the DLC campaign before the battery got too low. It was charging using the plane's USB but it looks like the Switch 2 draws more power than what that port could provide. Towards the end of the flight I played some Balatro since it's not graphics heavy. That game is still so addicting every time. When in the hotel room I plan on wrapping up remaining side quests in Everspace 2. On the plane ride back I intend to spend it giving proper time to Tape to Tape (Switch 2). We'll see. It's also a little chilly here for my SoCal bones.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. I’m going to beat the Golf Champion this weekend.

1. Ocarina of Time (Switch 2). Very fun game, right into the feelings sometimes, also I love the world and character building. It feels so much more alive than the N64 game. I don't rate games I haven't finished yet, but it's going to be somewhere between 9,60 and 9,89, possibly the highest rating I have ever given a console game. (Current Zelda series top score is BotW with a 9,725)

2. Fire Emblem Fortunes Weave. I absolutely love this game, and I haven't yet finished all acts 1. Game is sitting firmly at the Fire Emblem best score of a 9,20-9,35. (because also not finished)

And 4. Guild Wars Reforged (PC). Only game ever gotten a 9,910 rating. And currently highest scoring game. And they just announced new DLC for the first time in 20 years, so..

Bought OoT and have started playing it for the first time in my life (Never owned an N64). Such a beautiful remake.

Also started Dispatch on my PC through Amazon Luna.

Ocarina of Time is my Christmas present so I will continue my playthroughs of Super Mario Galaxy 2 and Pokemon Soul Silver.

Might get some Switch Sports Resort in too.Have a good weekend everyone!

#4133. Phantom Blade Zero kicks off its launch with a day one patch that offers improvements to ray tracing and some bug fixes to boot

If you've been hankering for some video gamey wuxia shenanigans, today seems like a good day for it, given that Phantom Blade Zero has now been released unto the world (with a 145GB install size that's technically actually 300GB but only for a bit). And like many big games before it, it comes not quite finished, as a day one patch attends to some of the action game's issues… I think, anyway, there's been a promise of a day one patch but no clear indicator if it's actually arrived or not. I don't own it either, so I can't check. At least I can tell you what's in it!

According to this Steam blog post, the update adds on a whole extra 5GB, claiming to significantly improve "ray tracing and path tracing performance," and offer "several bug fixes. If you’ve already pre-loaded the game, please download and install the update before launching. If you haven’t pre-loaded, your download will automatically include the latest version." That does more or less make it sounds like the patch is already here, there just aren't any patch notes to go with it.

The post goes on to explain that the team has "spent a great deal of time refining the game’s rasterized visuals so that each environment stays true to our art direction even with ray tracing turned off." It should also work on mid-range and lower-end PCs, and handhelds too, though on the game's discussions page and elsewhere I have spotted some folks facing some trouble.

Last point on the post also states that they've "observed some performance instability with NVIDIA’s latest 621.01 driver. Based on our testing, version 617.42 currently offers the best experience in Phantom Blade Zero. If you’ve installed a driver newer than 617.42, we recommend rolling back to 617.42 and choosing the clean installation option. Please stay on this version until NVIDIA releases its next driver update, which we expect to arrive soon."

Essentially, nothing that sounds like a massive dealbreaker just yet, so, happy Phantom Blade Zeroing I guess!

#4132. 007 First Light's First Mission Is Free in New PS5 Starter Pack

IO Interactive has announced a Starter Pack for 007 First Light will be released on the PS Store in the coming days that lets all PS5 owners play the game's introductory mission for free.

The download will be available from 10th November 2026 on PS5, and grants access to the Against the Odds level at the start of the campaign. In this mission, you'll be introduced to the world and the style of gameplay IO Interactive went for after Hitman 3.

It's a nice taster of what's to come in the full game, and if you like what you play, then your progress will carry over if you decide to purchase it. 007 First Light has also just been added to PS Plus Premium, where you can play it for an hour. That should let you play a little bit beyond the first mission.

Making the offer even better, 007 First Light is discounted as part of the PS Store Black Friday sale. The Deluxe Edition is available at 50% off for £34.99 / $39.99, until 21st November 2026.

Review 007 First Light (PS5) - James Bond Returns in a Strong, Confident Origin Adventure

You'll get to try one of 2026's best PS5 games, as we said in our 007 First Light PS5 review: "The characterisation of this young Bond and his associates is really strong, and the globetrotting story lets you explore some great locations. It really shines in its sandbox missions, but it weaves these together with its more linear moments in a seamless, cinematic way."

Will you give 007 First Light a go via this Starter Pack next week? Let us know in the comments below.

#4131. Mouthwashing is getting a feature film adaptation from Sony and I need all of you to be normal about it whenever it comes out

I quite liked that there video game Mouthwashing. It had a lot to say about how corporations take advantage of their workers, it played around with character perspective to let you in on certain narrative threads and withhold others until they're taut enough to snap, and was short enough so that its misery didn't outstay its welcome. What I wasn't so fond of was much of the fandom response that came afterwards, which is why I am quite scared to say that it's getting a movie from Sony.

As shared by The Hollywood Reporter, Sony have acquired the feature film rights to Mouthwashing, attaching names both promising and apprehension inducing to it. It's being produced in part by Scott Derrickson, director of Sinister (which I liked well enough) and Doctor Strange (a wet fart sound of a movie). What is more interesting is that Karyn Kusama, director of the excellent cult classic Jennifer's Body, is attached to direct. Given the game's themes of sexual assault, which is putting it lightly, it's nice to see a woman in the director's seat.

YES, MOUTHWASHING MOVIE IS REALLY HAPPENING SOON™ You thought you could escape responsibility by turning off your console? Produced by Sony Pictures' Screen Gems and directed by Karyn Kusama.[image or embed]

The thing that loops me back around to fear is having Matt Manfredi and Phil Hay attached as writers; the pair have long worked together, but often on stinkers like Clash of the Titans, The Tuxedo, and R.I.P.D. At the very least the two of them and Kusama are frequent collaborators, having made The Invitation and Destroyer together (it probably helps that Hay and Kusama are married).

As with every single live action adaptation of a video game, I of course immediately feel that it is wholly unnecessary, and certainly think that's the case for Mouthwashing. It's a game that has minimal interactivity, much more of a walking sim than anything else. It also deeply relies on said interactivity, alongside its first-person perspective, so I'm not sure how well that would translate. And upsettingly, the game developed an uncomfortably intense fandom that has frequently treated the game's themes as a suggestion, prioritising skits and memes above a real reckoning with what it's doing. This leaves me afraid of a film adaptation. Perhaps I'll log off for the day whenever it comes out.

#4130. Hideo Kojima Is 'Inventing A New Medium' - Bill Skarsgård Shares Why Starring In Xbox's PHYSINT Is A 'Big Deal'

"I think Kojima is a pioneer, and keeps going out to untrodden waters"

Hideo Kojima always brings a certain sense of mystery and allure to his work, as is currently the case with the OD KNOCK and PHYSINT projects. For quite some time, speculation over who would star in the latter threw all sorts of crazy names into the mixer, before Kojima revealed that Pennywise and Dune actor Bill Skarsgård had got the job.

Skarsgård recently appeared on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, where he spoke about how working with Hideo Kojima is a "big deal" for him. He also admitted that he grew up playing all the Metal Gear Solid games and is a big fan of Kojima's process.

"I played every single one [Metal Gear Solid], at least the ones on platform. So, I was very enamoured by him and the sort of the mythology or the universes that he creates, but also the sort of mystique and allure about him as well."

As the actor continued to praise the Metal Gear creator, Skarsgård seemed to specifically be impressed by Kojima's fluent knowledge of filmmaking despite being a video game developer. He even recalled a moment where he asked Kojima if he would ever make a film:

"[Kojima] is an auteur, but he's a video game auteur. He's fluent in filmmaking, in film, and in cinema. I remember at one point, way back 20 years ago, there was talk about doing a Metal Gear Solid movie, and, is gonna Hideo gonna direct it? I asked him, 'would you ever do a film?' and he's like 'no'. At this point, what he's doing is inventing a new medium."

Skarsgård touched briefly on his performance capture in PHYSINT and suggested he's working on eight hours of narrative storytelling.

"What we're gonna do is eight hours worth of narrative, right? But it's also an entire universe that you play, so it truly is quite literally world building. But now with technology, we're getting closer and closer to something that's photorealistic, but it's also interactive when you play it. I think he's a pioneer, and keeps going out to untrodden waters."

PHYSINT is a return to tactical espionage for Kojima since departing Konami and Metal Gear Solid in 2015. We're very excited to see what he's been cooking up with Bill and the rest of the cast when we eventually learn more. Xbox has also remained fairly quiet on how PHYSINT fits into Microsoft's exclusivity plans.

#4129. Baldur's Gate 3 custom campaign mod channels World of Warcraft with an adventure about undead former slaves fighting to reclaim a kingdom

From the creator of the Act Two Expansion mod which came out in September

The opening act of a Baldur's Gate 3 custom campaign mod which injects an adventure set in the World of Warcraft universe into Larian's RPG has been released. The mod, Forsaken, is another ambitious bit of work from a modder who recently expanded the second act of BG3's main story with a new region to explore before you head into the final chapter. This time, they've abandoned the D&Dverse for a tale of undead slaves rising up after being freed from serving a Lich King.

"You play as one of the Forsaken; an Undead who has recently awakened to find they are no longer slaves to the Lich King," modder SquallyDaBeanz wrote of Forsaken, their latest creation to release via Nexus Mods. "Now you must find your place in this new world alongside other freed Undead as you fight to reclaim the kingdom of Lordaeron. Hunt fierce beasts, explore forgotten ruins, end dark rituals, slay zealots, discover magical items, and more in this Custom Campaign for levels 1-5."

This campaign's setting is based on the Tirisfal Glades region seen in both World of Warcraft's classic and vanilla versions, with the mod being deliberately disconnected from the world of Baldur's Gate and SquallyDaBeanz even having aimed to emulate WOW's design philosophy. The initial release only features Forsaken's first act, but there's still plenty to do within that.

More than 20 quests await across a map that the modder said is designed to feel as expansive as World of Warcraft usually does, while offering a good deal of things to discover despite it not being as tightly packed with locations and secrets as vanilla BG3's professionally crafted locales. There are some towns, settlements, and dungeons to run across as you adventure with a party of up to three specially-built companions. The trio - a fighter named Darnell, a mage called Isabella and a cleric named Duesten - can be found in a charming-sounding place dubbed Deathknell Chapel. "The current implementation is temporary and exists purely to have a full party for combat encounters," SquallyDaBeanz noted of these companions. "A complete overhaul is in the works but I chose to put it off for a future update."

While there are NPCs and traders to chat with, the current version of the mod's quite heavily focused on combat and is fairly linear compared to vanilla BG3. Though, that has seemed to be the case with a lot of BG3 custom campaign mods I've covered thus far, especially those that are still works-in-progress like Forsaken.

Going forwards, SquallyDaBeanz hasn't provided an estimate as to when the mod'll be getting a second act, but has laid out some features they plan to add to the opening act in future. More quests, class dialogue, skill checks, items, and lore books are all on the to-do list, as well as adding idle animations and cutscenes for some NPCs.

If you fancy giving Forsaken a go, you'll need to nab its main file and install it with help from the instructions in the mod's description. Then, once you've enabled Forsaken via BG3's in-game mod manager found in the main menu, you'll need to start a new game to be whisked off to WOWville.

Netflix marks the first Stranger Things Day since the show ended with a blooper reel

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

In celebration of Stranger Things Day 2026, Netflix has released the season 5 blooper reel over 10 months after the show ended, but fans were expecting more.

The new clip, posted on Twitter by the official Stranger Things account, gives us a behind-the-scenes look at Millie Bobby Brown, Finn Wolfhard, Noah Schnapp, Caleb McLaughlin, Natalia Dyer, Maya Hawke, and more messing up their lines and riffing off one another while filming the final season. It is especially fun to see Vecna star Jamie Campbell Bower act so normal while in full prosthetics. But the stars of the reel have to be Gaten Matarazzo and Joe Keery, whose off-screen relationship is just as sweet as their characters Dustin and Steve's on-screen dynamic. Watch the full video below.

ROLL THE ST5 BLOOPER REEL 🎞️ #StrangerThingsDay https://t.co/FHr5rBPj2ONovember 6, 2026

It looks like the gang had a lot of fun while shooting the sci-fi show's saddest installment. But in the replies, it sounds like fans were expecting more from the first Stranger Things Day since the show ended. "There better be something bigger coming later," commented one fan, and another added, "Now give me the rest."

Fans are still a little salty about how the series ended. When the final episode aired on New Year's Day, some viewers refused to accept the ending, theorizing that a secret ninth episode was on the way. This was known as Conformity Gate. Fans went through the season and picked out mistakes and 'clues' that looked to suggest that the finale was just a ruse set up by Vecna, believing that the real finale was on the way.

Then, when Netflix teased that something was coming on January 7, fans caused the site to crash while waiting for a new episode. But nothing appeared. Instead, Netflix posted a teaser for its trailer for its 2026 slate, seemingly bringing Conformity Gate to an end. But some fans are still holding out hope that the show isn't over yet.

Stranger Things Day is celebrated every year on November 6, which marks the day that Will Byers went missing in Hawkins in 1983. Byers was abducted by a Demogorgon in the very first season's first episode, causing a chain of events that would threaten the very end of the world, which all comes to a head in Stranger Things season 5.

Stranger Things is available to watch in its entirety on Netflix. For more, check out our guide to the best Netflix shows, and keep up with new shows on the way.

#4126. There are no more Assassin's Creed remakes in development, because Ubisoft are focused on Hexe, Invictus and "projects you haven't heard about yet"

They're still updating Black Flag Resynced, however, and bringing NG+ to Valhalla

Ubisoft have announced that they aren't working on any more Assassin's Creed remakes for the moment, despite learning a "tremendous amount" from Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced. Instead, it's all shoulders to the wheel for a thrilling future that contains witches, a stronger sense of narrative cohesion, and possibly some kind of Assassin's Creed Smash Bros equivalent. In the shorter term, Ubisoft are still adding things to both Resynced and Assassin's Creed Valhalla.

The news comes as part of a fireside chat from Jean Guesdon, head of content. After offering libations to Assassin's Creed's new leadership team - in particular Martin Schelling, former Assassin's Creed: Revelations producer and nowadays, head of brand – he shares the results of a survey about whatpeople currently want from Assassin's Creed at large. Ubisoft's three takeaways are that players would like them to communicate more, work harder to shore up Assassin's Creed's "unique identity", and create "a more coherent narrative that respects and expands Assassin's Creed's lore."

All of which is basically telling us nothing, though I'm interested to hear thoughts from old AC stalwarts about where the frame story of Assassin vs Templar has gone off the rails. I feel like "incoherent" is AC's default state and a significant part of its charm. Ubisoft are going to do further closed-doors workshops about the future of the series with certain big cheeses in the AC fanbase, via Discord.

The post includes news of changes to existing Assassin's Creeds. Black Flag Resynced has just been updated with a New Game+ mode, a "nightmare" difficulty setting, some takedown animations, and some fresh cosmetics. Resynced's older/younger sibling Assassin's Creed Valhalla is also getting a New Game+ mode, out 5th November, which introduces a new optional progression system, more resources for upgrades, a new gear quality level, a stash system, and some cosmetics.

There's a section on Codename Invictus, Ubisoft's unrevealed multiplayer Assassin's Creed project, which had a closed playtest featuring a new prototype a few months ago. Ubisoft say people like the PvP, parkour, map verticality, and range of AC characters.

"One piece of feedback came through clearly though: players saw great potential in the foundations but wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed," Guesdon writes. "The team spent the past months acting on it, and Invictus is now evolving in an exciting direction that better reflects those pillars while staying true to its multiplayer ambitions." I quite enjoyed Assassin's Creed's first efforts at multiplayer, in which players posed as NPCs on crowded maps, but as a Doubting Thomas, I also suspect Invictus is some kind of suffocating live service kraken. I suspect this is what the unnamed playtesters meant by wanting "more of the pillars".

I am more interested to hear about Codename Hexe, Ubisoft's other big forthcoming Creedojaunt, even though Clint Hocking is no longer working on it. It's reportedly a witch fable set during the time of the Holy Roman Empire. They'll be telling us more about that next year, Guesdon says.

Finally - well, apart from some flannel about the AC Netflix series and the series' 20th anniversary next year - there's a paragraph about remakes. "One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development," Guesdon writes. "Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories. But don't mistake that for a closed door. Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back."

Some context for all this: Ubisoft recently made layoffs at Resynced studio Ubisoft Singapore, in the course of wider cost-cutting after an injection of funds from Tencent. In May, company boss Yves Guillemot told investors that the coming financial year would be a "low point", promising healthier returns from Assassin's Creed, Far Cry and Ghost Recon by early 2029.

I didn't play Resynced, and I'm mixed on remakes at large. I like remakes when they are effectively brand new games that happen to be retelling a familiar story, and having fun with it: games like Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, which are in ferocious dialogue with the original. But remakes that are just about stuffing the mechanics into Unreal Engine 5 and grafting on some progression and crafting mechanics? It's just feeding ash to the fire. What's your mileage?

#4125. Xbox's New PC App Update Is Impressive, Even If There's A Few Teething Problems

Just yesterday, Microsoft began rolling out an update for the Xbox PC app, making it faster and more responsive on Windows desktop and handheld. We've had a little play with the new version, and our first impressions are mostly positive.

Xbox boss Asha Sharma posted a short video showing off the boot speed of the revamped Xbox PC app. It took a mere 5.2 seconds to load into the home page, clocking in a full 10 seconds quicker than the current version.

Having tried the new Xbox PC app ourselves, we can confirm that it's noticeably faster than the current version. It opens wonderfully swift on my Windows 10 desktop, stocked with 64GB of Sam Altman's precious FU-RAM, but it's also pretty nippy on my first-gen ASUS ROG Ally.

It was important to me that this new version worked well on my ROG Ally, because the current one takes an age to boot in the handheld's 15W Windows mode. I've never enjoyed that feeling of being forced to switch the ROG Ally into Performance or Turbo mode just to get the Xbox PC app running. Now, I don't have to. Big W for this update!

Beyond the speed improvements, the new app looks so much cleaner and feels much more in line with the Xbox console experience, which has been something I've always hoped we'd see: a kinda merger between the PC and Xbox console interfaces, with the latter serving as more of a base.

The side bar is much slicker too. Social stuff like who's online and what they're up to now display alongside Home, Library, Game Pass, and Store options. Cloud Gaming has been removed from the left-hand bar though, which made it a little awkward to access.

I found launching a game via the cloud a bit confusing. Almost like it's been hidden on purpose. I expected to be able to head to a cloud-enabled title, open its game page, and find the button to launch it via the cloud. Just like before. However, there's nothing to select. It simply says "I own this". Instead, I had to head back to the library page, hit Select, open the submenu, and choose "Play on Cloud". It's handy, but took a little searching to get working.

Remote Play has also been tucked away in a dropdown menu for some reason. I'd much rather see it on the left, alongside the other main tab options. I reckon with a bit more time the new Xbox PC app will be fantastic, and with a couple of updates it should work out some of the kinks I mentioned above.

The first look at Latveria in Avengers: Doomsday is here over a month early – as part of a Jeep commercial.

As spotlighted by New Rockstars' Erik Voss on Twitter, the latest round of Doomsday marketing features Captain America, Johnny Storm, and The Thing each taking a Jeep through a portal in a handful of familiar locations – including Avengers Tower and Wakanda.

The Avengers Doomsday tie-in commercials keep showing us interesting world details from the film. Here's our first-ever look at LATVERIA in the MCU! Doctor Doom's towering Doomstadt castle towers over the city in the mountains of Eastern Europe. Hey, thanks Jeep! https://t.co/DQHZFZEihNNovember 5, 2026

Their final destination is the real talking point, however. There, the Jeeps converge into the snowy climes of Latveria, a mountainous nation-state that appears to show Doom's castle and the capital Doomstadt.

In the comics, Castle Doom is frequently depicted as Doctor Doom's base of operations, upon which he rules over the fictional nation of Latveria. But much like most of Doomsday, Doom's HQ has been under wraps.

#4123. Helldivers 2 boss can "absolutely see" making a game parody of generative AI, but it would need to be "quirky" rather than "doom-laden"

Arrowhead's chief creative officer Johan Pilestedt can well imagine the Helldivers studio developing a videogame that satirises or parodies today's generative AI technology. The game in question wouldn't be a Helldivers project, however, and Pilestedt says it would need to be relatively upbeat, rather than an exercise in feverish despair. This seems like a tall order right now, at least while Tim Sweeney still has access to Twitter.

"AI has been worth parodying since the ‘80s, and I can absolutely see a game where you’re stuck in a world with an AI overlord that’s basically a deity," Pilestedt told me during an interview on the company's future. "But the Automatons already cover our robot enemy needs in Helldivers 2, so if we went there, it would be a new title, and we’d want to frame it in a quirky, fun way rather than a doom-laden one."

The aim to keep things light is consistent, of course, with how Helldivers approaches satire. "Not everyone gets it, but plenty of players love playing along with the joke," Pilestedt commented elsewhere in our chatathon, with regard to how Helldivers portrays fascism. "The humor doesn't hide the message, it delivers it."

While robotic, Helldivers 2's Automatons aren't a commentary on generative AI. They're broadly a spoof of Soviet Russia, red star imagery and all, if Soviet Russia had happened to be populated by Terminators. Based on the secessionist planet of Cyberstan, the Automatons are led by a group of Cyborgs who are waging war partly out of revenge for Super Earth's efforts to "euthanise" them. Still, perhaps there's scope to patch in more present-day parallels and upgrade the Automatons from cosy T-1000 analogues into something redolent of, say, Krafton's plans to use game data for unpiloted weapon systems.

Any satire of genAI Arrowhead make would need to reckon with the fact that Arrowhead appear open to making use of the technology, within limits. “I find that anything that is [an] AI-related debate in the games industry ends up being on both ends of the spectrum," Arrowhead CEO Shams Jorjani told The Game Business in an interview last year. "Either we have Square Enix executives talking about 77% being automated through QA, or we have developers who feel that... the very fabric of their being is being threatened and therefore all AI is bad AI. Maybe could it be that reality is somewhere in the middle?"

Jorjani contrasted fears about job losses to generative AI with less anxious reaction to older automation middleware such as Simplygon, while conceding that Simplygon isn't on the same "massive scale" as generative AI tools. He also stressed that "we need to make sure that we're not stealing people's intellectual property and rights".

Pilestedt didn't share his own opinions about generative AI during our conversation - in his defence, I didn't ask for them specifically. He did, however, talk about why Arrowhead's current unannounced project isn't Helldivers 3 - briefly, they don't want to "reset" the momentum of Helldivers 2.

#4122. Composer shares 20 minutes of music created for Mass Effect 5 following tragic closure of BioWare

Austin Wintory has shared twenty minutes of music they pitched to BioWare and EA in hopes of joining the Mass Effect 5 development team, following the tragic closure of BioWare last week.

The composer, known for his work on Journey and Sword of the Sea, uploaded the music to his personal YouTube channel. It was made without knowledge of the narrative direction of the new Mass Effect game, but was presented as a surprise to the companies in 2025 as part of years of conversation. Wintory writes in the video that it was a "direct homage" to Mass Effect 1 composers Jack Wall and Sam Hulick, leaning into analog synths and "a more complex integration of the orchestra", a hybrid approach Wintory compares to The Matrix movies scores.

This collection of music includes a track called The Legacy of Shepard, which includes "deliberate winks" to the original Mass Effect theme. The second track - Sailing the Relays - features the blend of synth and orchestra mentioned earlier quite heavily. All in all, there are eight tracks included in total, with the eighth being a remix of that first Legacy of Shepard composition.

The video's description contains a sombre message on BioWare's closure, as well as gratitude towards the music departments involved in the conversations Wintory took part it: "Receiving the news alongside everyone else that EA had decided to not only cancel the project but shutdown BioWare entirely was a deeply felt loss. It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever.

"Thank you nonetheless to everyone at BioWare and EA's music department for gifting me the chance to dream in your sandbox. It was a privilege to do even that much."

Wintory is not alone in their sadness. EA's closure of BioWare, which included the firing of 50 employees and a further 350 across other EA-owned studios, many across the industry came forward to decry the decision. The decision may even have political ramifications, as one Canadian party leader has expressed a desire to allow BioWare employees to buy back the studio with federal support. This all happened shortly after EA's $55bn private acquisition from Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and Saudi Arabia's Savvy Games Group.

#4121. Rockstar developer union could end up over 1,600 workers strong and encompass nearly all UK staff below senior management, IWGB claim

Organisers say a successful vote would create "the biggest recognised union in the UK games sector"

As we've previously covered, a vote on recognition of a union made up of UK-based Rockstar Games devs is set to take place around GTA 6's console launch on November 19th. The Independent Workers of Great Britain (IWGB) union, whom the Rockstar staff are working with in their efforts to organise, have now revealed just how many workers the Rockstar could end up encompassing if the recognition vote is successful. It's not a small number.

As reported by Game File, when asked to put a number on their claim that the vote could result in "the biggest recognised union in the UK games sector", the IWGB said that the union’s bargaining unit would be made up of more than 1,600 workers. That, according to the union, is nearly everyone at Rockstar's UK studios below the director level. The director level's typically corpospeak for senior management, or the point at which you go from regular staff to the lowest rungs of the exec ladder which leads all the way up to the biggest of gold-plated desks.

Naturally, this UK Rockstar union won't include Rockstar staff based in other studios across the world, including the US and India. Recent reporting from Bloomberg cited Rockstar's total staff number as being over 4,700 people in 12 places across the globe.

The UK union recognition votes will be held from November 12th, a week before GTA 6's console launch, and November 26th.

"For me, this vote comes down to ensuring employees at Rockstar get honesty and openness surrounding the decisions that affect them," Rockstar Game Workers Union Committee Member Shanti Easton-Steel said in a press release issued by IWBG earlier this week. "When management choices are kept hidden, we can’t properly address issues like the gender pay gap, the uneven and ever-changing policies on overtime pay, or the concerns many co-workers hold around job security post-release."

Also set to come to a head around the time GTA 6 plops onto consoles is the employment tribunal which has seen Rockstar and the IWGB butt heads over the former's decision to fire 34 mostly UK-based staffers last year. Rockstar have accused the fired staff of risking the leaking of confidential info while posting on a Discord server set up by union organisers. The IWGB have accused Rockstar of being motivated by a desire to union bust.

#4119. Xbox Publisher Announces Four Games Being Delisted By End Of 2026

All set to disappear in a few weeks' time

It's never good news when games get delisted on the Xbox Store, but we haven't actually got many for the end of 2026 as things stand, and at least we're getting some notice on the four titles that are set to be removed.

All of these games are coming from one publisher - GameMill Entertainment. Their games can be very hit-and-miss, but most of them involve some pretty big IP, and I've enjoyed my time with a few of them in the past.

The four games they will be delisting on Xbox very soon are as follows:

The delist announcement for all four of these games was shared on Steam, and it only mentions Steam. However, GameMill has done this kind of thing before, and it's usually resulted in delistings for multiple platforms including Xbox.

As for whether they're worth it? Well, Avatar: The Last Airbender - Quest for Balance doesn't exactly have the best reputation, while childish platformer Hotel Transylvania 3 only fares slightly better. Street Outlaws 2 is considered the better of the two and certainly looks intriguing, but still has mixed impressions based on what we've seen.

Honestly, you shouldn't be buying any of these games at full price in our view, but it's worth keeping an eye out to see if they get heavy discounts before the end of 2026. Street Outlaws 1 and 2 have already been reduced by 90% on Steam ahead of their delistings, and we reckon the same thing might happen on Xbox in the near future.

Use the latest Shibuya codes if you want a chance to reroll your Clan, Race, or Cursed Technique

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Shibuya codes grant a bunch of free rerolls in a variety of categories, giving you the chance to reroll your Race, Clan, and Cursed Technique whenever you want. All three of the categories have some incredible rare and mythical options, and of course your chances of rolling them are super low, so the more rerolls you have, the better.This Jujutsu Kaisen-inspired Roblox game is an RPG experience in which you put yourself into the shoes of a human or a cursed spirit - with rerolls, you also have a chance to become one of a few roll-exclusive clans, too. To live the virtual life you want, you'll need as many rerolls as possible to customize your character to your exact requirements, so here are the latest Shibuya codes to help you do just that. If you're after some more general avatar rewards to use in all of your experiences, then we've got the current Roblox promo codes covered too.

These are the Shibuya codes you can redeem right now:

Shibuya codes almost always offer rerolls, but they are specific to the character you're customizing at the time you redeem them, so if you have more than one character slot, be careful to redeem codes where you want them.It's also worth noting that Shibuya codes aren't case-sensitive, so you only have to make sure the spelling is correct, but you can always just copy and paste from the list above if you want to be safe.

To redeem Shibuya codes, you must be in the character customization screen for the character you want the rewards to apply to. To get here from in-game, double click the Menu button at the top of the screen. This is the same menu you'll see when you load into the game.

From here, select Slots, then choose the character you want to apply your codes to and click Customize. If you only have one character, it'll automatically select them for you. From the customization screen, you'll see the codes redemption box in the top right-hand corner. Type or copy your code into the enter code box and hit enter to claim your rewards.

Shibuya codes expire fairly quickly, so it's always worth redeeming them as soon as you see them. Since your Rerolls stack and don't expire, there's no harm in doing so. Whenever promos do expire, I'll move them down here so you don't experience any disappointment.

#4116. Pokémon Unite closing down for good, but you'll still be able to use it afterwards, sort of

That's it for Pokémon Unite. Tencent's once-popular MOBA is being switched off in March 2027. The Pokémon Company announced the news today, saying: "We regret to inform you that service for Pokémon Unite will end on Tuesday, March 23, 2027, at 00:00 UTC."

By way of thanking people for playing, a "special event" runs from now until service-end, which brings a number of additions to the game. Among them is an intriguing Library feature that lets you continue using the game, to a degree, after its end.

The Library allows you to access the Practice Area of Pokémon Unite to view your earned items - Holowear, cosmetics, Pokémon, and achievements - so your efforts in the game won't entirely disappear. It'll be available starting 12th November. But note that you'll need to use the Library before the 23rd March 2027 switch-off date to get the data Library needs to show your achievements, and because that data's stored locally, you may lose the data if you change device.

"Library data generally cannot be transferred when changing devices," the Pokémon website said. "If the game or library data is deleted or otherwise lost after service ends, it may not be recoverable. Support for the library feature will not be available after service ends."

It seems like a thoughtful way to sunset a game, allowing players a record of their progress and some interactivity, instead of yanking everything away entirely.

Pokémon Unite launched in 2021, first on Switch and then on mobile devices. It's a free-to-play MOBA, essentially, where two teams of five battle it out in an arena with various routes through it and control points to secure and, as Pokémon battle, they earn experience and level up. Pokémon Unite had already been shut down in some European countries because of loot box gambling concerns.

#4115. Opinion: Hey, That Hellraiser: Revival Game Is Pretty Good

For as much as I love the horror genre, I've never seen a Hellraiser film. If they're as fun to watch as Hellraiser: Revival is to play, though, then maybe I need to catch up.

Since we've got The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and GTA 6 right around the corner (I'm now playing the former), I haven't wanted to start a big game that requires a serious time investment. With a 10-hour playthrough for the Platinum Trophy (which I did earn), this new Hellraiser game seemed like the perfect fit.

This is a straightforward, mostly linear survival horror game that gets in and out without overstaying its welcome. It shows touches of flair and ambition at some points, with light takes on the more open-ended Resident Evil approach to exploration, providing a little area to progress through. Those moments are cool, and in between them is action, puzzle-solving, horror, sex, and the Labyrinth.

You know me by now: I love survival horror and all the typical trappings of the genre. When it wants to — a few times during the campaign — Hellraiser: Revival does them adequately enough. It's no Resident Evil or Silent Hill killer, so what I've loved most about the game are the factors you'd stereotypically associate with the IP: chains, Pinhead, telekinesis, and the Labyrinth.

Main character Aidan and his girlfriend Sunny decide to use a Genesis Configuration cube during sex, but activating the thing calls upon Pinhead and his cronies, interrupting the intimacy (of which there is a lot). Sunny is taken hostage and Aidan has to fight back through guns, melee weapons, and the Genesis Configuration.

This elaborate puzzle box grants him telekinesis powers, and later, the ability to wield fireballs.

The mechanic is a standout, and presents a welcome alternative to stabbing and blasting guys and gals in gimp masks.

You can summon saw blades, spikes, and sharp debris and throw them at zombies and cultists. If you see a brazier, you can steal its fire and lob it at enemies. With the blaze it creates, you can create more fireballs from the burnt remains. It is a neat little system that I thoroughly enjoyed, and would love to see expanded should there ever be a sequel.

My favourite sequences overall, though, took place in the Labyrinth. In this alternate realm, you face spike traps, moving saws, contorting paths and staircases, and demons like the Chatterer that chase you. Also requiring you to move blocks with your telekinesis powers under a time pressure, these sequences are genuinely intense. You can feel the Chatterer stalking you as its teeth, well, chatter.

Is Hellraiser: Revival a hidden gem that should be claiming Game of the Year nominations? No.

Viewing the Metacritic page for a gauge of its critical reception at launch, I think an overall rating of 69 to 76, depending on what platform you're playing on, is bang on. If I were reviewing Hellraiser: Revival, with my critic cap on, I don't think I could score it any higher than a 7/10.

However, I've been playing Hellraiser: Revival for fun rather than my job, and that's exactly what I've had: fun.

I want to see more from this universe; I hope Saber Interactive gives the green light to a sequel.

In the meantime, I'll go and catch up on those movies.

Have you played Hellraiser: Revival since it launched for PS5 last month? What did you make of the game? Let me know if you agree with my opinion in the comments below.

#4114. Splendid Junji Ito-inspired RPG World of Horror is now 20% more horrible, thanks to a free PC update with extra gods, locations, and wounds

This hole was already made for me, but now it's a fair bit wider and deeper

Excellent apocalypse RPG World of Horror has just received a sizeable free update, As Below So Above, adding no less than two Old Godly invasions for you to identify and thwart. One of these additional cosmic disasters involves four cults summoning their fave abominations at the same time. I picture them forming a shaky barbershop quartet on the skyline, while stamping the streets to mush. Damn it, Ath-Yolazsth – you're leading again!

Also in As Below So Above: more "enemies, mysteries, characters, items, spells, curses, and injuries", together with "a large batch of quality-of-life features and bug fixes". I can only applaud the vicious disconnect of listing "injuries" alongside "quality-of-life". These will be the most polished and ergonomic grievous wounds you've ever had! The experience will flow like your gushing blood!

This is the Junji Ito-inspired game's largest update yet, according to developers panstasz and publishers Ysbryd. It makes the game 20% bigger, though surely no mere percentage can ever encapsulate the creatures and forces that slumber on the other side of the mortal veil.

"Two never-before-seen manifestations of the Old Gods raise the stakes," explains the press release. "IKT-YOSIS, THE FIRST NIGHTMARE, sleeps in a gargantuan chamber beneath the mountains. With each ritual performed to wake him, the world above slowly reshapes itself and brings strange weather with it." You'll need to keep tabs on forecasts, if you want to get ahead of the elements. As for "THE WAR FOR SHIOKAWA", this "adds an extra level of terror, with four cults summoning their eldritch masters simultaneously to plunge the town into pure evil."

It's just as well there are three new puny human protagonists to continue the battle against these cyclopean trouble-makers: Kiriko, who knows her way around a Tarot deck, Satoshi, a seasoned hiker, and Makoto, a school AV club member. You'll also be able to enlist 10 additional allies and learn about them care of a reworked conversation system, which trips at random between investigations.

There's a new location, the Mountains, alongside 60 extra events, 19 enemies, three challenges, and 30 items. And let's not forget the Scenario Mode, which plays host to self-contained yarns set before the main game. The first of these Worldlets of Horror is a hunt for three students lost in the woods, with a variety of endings.

Lots of numbers! And while much of this may break your mind, none of it will break your mods. There's a new modding system that's backwards compatible with everything made for the 1.0 version.

Unfamiliar with World of Horror? Here is Alice Bee's review (RPS in peace): "Repetitive combat in World Of Horror can't entirely mar a unique, stylish and layered horror adventure that makes you want to play more the more that you play."

#4113. Fan favourite map Shipment arrives today in Modern Warfare 4, just four days after launch - a new record for Call of Duty

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is getting a small update today that includes the latest iteration of Infinity Ward's iconic Shipment map. The map arrives just four days after Modern Warfare 4's launch last Friday, 23rd October, which is unusually quickly.

Shipment is the original Call of Duty 'small map'. First introduced in Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare in 2007, the map is designed to offer a breakneck pace of combat no other multiplayer map could. Though there have been Shipment-like small maps over the years - chiefly Treyarch's infamous Nuketown in the Black Ops sub-franchise - nothing could quite replicate Shipment's dizzying rhythm of mayhem.

Shipment's arrival in Modern Warfare 4 was expected, of course; the developer even announced the 27th October release date in a blog post prior to launch. However, joining the roster so close to the game's launch is notable.

Shipment typically arrives two or so weeks post-launch, usually in a game's first live service season. It's been part of Modern Warfare 2019, Modern Warfare 2 (2022), and Modern Warfare 3 (2023). A few other COD titles have versions inspired by it, though not entirely identical, such as COD: WW2's Shipment 1944.

It's long been assumed, perhaps cynically, that Shipment comes just as player numbers start falling off. As one of the series' most popular maps, the thinking is that bringing it back attracts a cohort of the audience who only play that map. It's often used to level up guns, and help get player levels up since the kill count is usually higher than in other, larger maps.

Indeed, Shipment typically releases alongside a dedicated, 24/7 playlist, meaning you don't have to hope for it to show up in the normal map rotation. Infinity Ward didn't say whether we can expect the same playlist this time around, though it is likely.

As with each new iteration, Modern Warfare 4 Shipment features the classic layout but in an entirely new environment inspired by locations from the game. This version has a more urban landscape look that takes after the very first version's muted colours, with Soviet-era concrete buildings in the background. The action takes place in a shipping yard by the harbour, among shipping containers, hence the name.

Incidentally, Modern Warfare 4 is also starting its first season early, with Season One kicking off 6th November, just two weeks after the game's launch, though it is curious Infinity Ward didn't wait until the season's launch to drop the map.

#4112. Gears Of War: E-Day Is Bringing Back Legacy Maps, Modes And Skins For Season 2

And tomorrow they’re giving away a free General RAAM skin!

The Coalition kicked off Gears' 20th anniversary celebrations by reviving a classic Versus mode, introducing a new Horde mission, and adding a few extra bits and bobs to Gears of War: E-Day.

It might not have seemed like much, but reintroducing Guardian to Versus was an excellent callback to the mode's debut in Gears of War 2. The game's first season is coming to a close at the end of November, making way for E-Day's Season 2 content: Legacy.

Tomorrow, E-Day players can claim a free General RAAM skin for multiplayer. All you have to do is log in - that's it. Season 2 begins on December 1st, promising to bring back fan-favourite maps, modes and skins to "honour the greatest hits of Gears over 20 years".

"And beginning December 1, we launch our next Season – titled Legacy – which continues to honor the greatest hits of Gears over 20 years in our maps, modes and multiplayer skins. Season 2 not only brings back some fan favorites from the history of the franchise but lets us reimagine characters in ways we’ve always wanted to see them – like Solemn Memories Dom, whose character skin depicts him in the suit he’s wearing in the famous photo of him and Maria from Gears of War 2."

Does this mean we're going to see Kalona's version of Gridlock, Blood Drive and Canals? I sure hope so! I'd also like to reunite the Carmine family in E-Day. Can you imagine a full squad of Carmines voiced by the one and only Michael Gough? I can, and I want it!

#4111. Phantom Blade Zero is asking players to free up 300GB of space for pre-loading, double its actual 145GB file size

Pre-loads are live for Phantom Blade Zero, the debut action game from Chinese developer S-Game. Alongside news of the pre-load, the studio revealed the final set of PC requirements, including how much space the game is going to take up on your drive.

Once installed, Phantom Blade Zero will occupy a chonky 145GB of your precious storage space. However, to pre-load the game, you're going to need over double that - 300GB, seemingly for the decryption and decompression process. The developer explained in a Steam blog post that "temporary files and the complete game files must coexist during the unlock process". You'll get back the extra space once the game is installed, of course.

While a game requiring extra space for these operations is not uncommon, the fact Phantom Blade Zero's install size is already so large makes needing to free up double that ludicrous. Phantom Blade Zero also requires an SSD drive, and seeing as the global gen-AI-driven memory and storage shortages have made them unattainable to many, you're not likely to buy a new drive just to accommodate a single game.

High as they may be, those storage space requirements aren't likely to deter players from buying a copy. Indeed, the game is already predicted to be among the year's biggest hits, having already sold over 500,000 copies on Steam alone, according to some estimates.

Eurogamer reviewed Phantom Blade Zero. In her review, Emma Kent was critical of the game's underwhelming boss flights and its general lack of polish, which she said mar Phantom Blade Zero's otherwise fluid and cinematic kung fu-style action.

Phantom Blade Zero arrives 29th October on PC and PS5.

#4110. EA execs choosing Star Wars Battlefront 3 over Mass Effect 5 was the main factor in BioWare's demise, according to report

Corporate chair shuffling and the Mass Effect studio's recent struggles may also have played roles

The postmortem on BioWare, following their shuttering by EA this month, points to the publisher's preference to back Star Wars Battlefront 3 over Mass Effect 5 as the main factor in the demise of the beloved RPG developer. That's according to Bloomberg, who also report that a couple of other factors likely also had some influence.

The Bloomberg report paints EA's position as being one of a company caught between spending a bunch of money on a Star Wars shooter-shaped rock and a hard place with a sign that read Mass Effect 5. Disney reportedly swooped in to offer the publishers the opportunity to make Star Wars Battlefront 3 around the time EA were, as a result of being saddled with debt as part of the leveraged buyout which saw the Saudi government and private equity take them over, looking to not to spend as much cash.

So, Star Wars and Mass Effect became a decision of whether Star Wars or Mass Effect would be the better bet to stick projected hundreds of millions of dollars on. The suits, quelle surprise really, went for the series that currently sits just below powerhouse money-maker Winnie the Pooh on Wikipedia's list of the highest-grossing media franchises. Battlefront 3's development reportedly hasn't even kicked off yet, but it's got that safe and predictable big name to it, and will be a shooter to nestle among EA's treasured flotilla of gun and ball games, rather than an RPG.

Bloomberg add that that BioWare's well-documented up and down record with game releases since Mass Effect: Andromeda began a skid which Anthem only made worse and Dragon Age: The Veilguard couldn't arrest also played a role. Potentially also in the mix was some corporate chair and nameplate switching among EA's execs this summer, which saw EA Sports-linked suits David Tinson and Cam Weber promoted while reported BioWare advocate Laura Miele was sidelined via promotion from overseeing EA's non-sports studios to a gig based around helping big boss Andrew Wilson pursue "strategic growth opportunities beyond EA's core business".

For what it's worth, an EA spokesperson told Bloomberg the company "collectively" decided to shoot BioWare into space "following months of planning, review, and analysis, including careful consideration of evolving business conditions, industry dynamics, and our long-term priorities".

And so, BioWare's body has been sent to the stars, while Respawn and DICE look set to make Battlefront 3. There is a bit of depressing irony in EA deciding to go for the perceived safe bet of a big name licensed game over taking some risk on a game that'd come without Disney as a rights-holding middleman. This is, after all, the company which in 2022 ditched governing body Fifa as the namesake and licensing partner of their very successful football games, choosing the risk of going it alone with a lesser brand EA would have more direct control over and ownership of rather than sticking with an established big name juggernaut.

Then again, you could probably call EA's soccer games something like 'Hey, you, person reading this: the (insert year here) football game you're looking at thinks your face is ugly and your haircut's stupid' and they'd still fly off the shelves.

#4109. Wooshy wuxia actioner Phantom Blade Zero is sharp enough on the Steam Machine, if blunted on the Steam Deck

It would appear that Phantom Blade Zero (Phantom Blade 0? Zero? Let’s go with Zero) demanding more gigs than a mismanaged stadium is doing little to stop people playing the thing. It therefore stands to reason at least some folks will want to run S-Game Studio’s lightly Soulsy sword-em-up on the Steam Machine, so let us now examine how said GabeCube stands up to its effects-heavy martial artistry. With some settings proposals, natch.

Two signs boded poorly, before I got to testing the Machine. The first was a comment on Oisin’s day one patch piece, warning of heavy glitching on a Linux system. The second was my Steam Deck OLED, also a Linux system, being incapable of running Phantom Blade Zero at even close to a steady 30fps; even with the Low preset and some nasty-looking Ultra Performance upscaling, the game’s flashy moves and jerking (apologies – cinematic) camera shifts made for regular framerate drops into the teens.

Fortunately, the Steam Machine is much more resilient, even if it does benefit from a few quality cuts (and, realistically, will struggle if pushed beyond standard 1080p.) The Medium preset and Quality-level FSR are enough for 45-60fps in what I’ve played so far, and the High preset – while a touch susceptible to sub-40fps dips for my liking – is at least playable without major bugs or stuttering.

Strangely enough, the only major technical problem I’ve had wasn’t caused by graphics, or the Linux-based SteamOS, but the Steam Controller I was playing with. Despite being assured during the boot process that I was being treated to the Official Gamepad Configuration – cor! – an unresponsive map-opening button left me immobile during a prompt tutorial. Immobile and, I suppose without a map, lost. It turns out this this is a common bug with the Steam Controller specifically, and can be fixed by remapping the Select button, in SteamOS’s controller settings, to emulate the effect of clicking the touchpad of a PS5 pad. PC gaming.

With that sorted, Phantom Blade Zero seems to work fine? If I was nitpicking I’d point out that some high-drama sequences are visibly less buttery than the slower, roaming sections, which can exceed 60fps on Medium. Same for a lot of cutscenes, which aren’t hard-locked to 30fps like prerendered scenes often are, but do cause heavy framerate drops for little apparent reason. Still, it’s reasonable when actually playing.

Settings-wise, that Medium preset (with FSR on Quality) works well if you’re lazy. But a few of Phantom Blade Zero’s individual quality options aren’t terribly performance-sapping by themselves, and than thus be tuned upwards for a slightly nicer-looking wuxia tale with minimal drawback. Have a crack with the following:

Don’t miss those Dynamic Resolution Quality and Super Resolution Output Scale tweaks; on their defaults, they both make the game uglier than it needs to be. And on the subject of Super Resolution, FSR upscaling does leave a bit of roughness on certain edges, but then at 1080p, so does FSR even when it’s on its Native Resolution setting. You might as well get the extra frames.

#4108. Nintendo is hosting a new Indie World showcase tomorrow, featuring games for Switch and Switch 2, and it'll be 15 minutes long

It's been a bumper year for Nintendo, with the likes of and Pokémon Pokopia kicking off 2026 in a very strong way for the company, and more recently with games like Fire Emblem and Nintendo Switch Sports Resort picking up strong scores for the platform holder.

But Nintendo still has more to come: today, the company announced a new Indie World Showcase. It'll take place tomorrow, 28th October and it will air at 7AM PT / 10AM ET/ 2PM GMT / 3PM CEST. The presentation will include games coming to both Switch 2 and the original Switch, and it will last for 15 minutes.

Join us on Oct 28 at 7am PT for a new #IndieWorld Showcase! Tune in for roughly 15 minutes of new announcements and updates on indie games coming to Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch.Watch here: https://t.co/yXkwvRMfTg pic.twitter.com/lwSQDXmdXk

The last Indie World Showcase we saw took place in March (and again, it was about 15 minutes long), and showed off titles like Mixtape, Toem 2, Blue Prince, Rotwood, Moonlighter 2, Denshattack, Blighted, Deadzone: Rogue, and more. These are the sort of titles you're to expect in tomorrow's showcase.

What are the big games that are going to be shown here? Now that Silksong has been released, there isn't the same fervour for Indie 'Directs' like this - but maybe we'll get shown something here that will incite that passion in gamers once again.

#4107. There's Demand to Remake Final Fantasy 6 from Within Square Enix, Says Series Boss

Could a remake of Final Fantasy 6 happen at some point? The idea's been floating around for a while, but we're now, apparently, at a point where Square Enix employees want to see it.

This is according to series veteran and current brand manager Yoshinori Kitase, who specifically notes that there's an internal demand for said remake while speaking to IGN.

The outlet asks Kitase for his thoughts on additional remake projects now that Final Fantasy 7 Remake's trilogy is coming to a close, and while he certainly doesn't commit to a definitive answer, his mention of Final Fantasy 6 is enough to raise eyebrows.

Kitase says that while he personally doesn't "have any particular feeling towards any kind of remake" at this moment in time, and that he doesn't believe he'll work on one "anytime soon", there's demand "inside the company".

"Inside the company and also among the Final Fantasy fans, there's been many people asking for a remake of Final Fantasy VI, so who knows?," he comments.

To me, this seems like the kind of seed that could sprout into something down the line. It's easy to forget that companies as big as Square Enix are seeing constant churn in terms of development teams and project leads; all it takes is for someone to gather support and pitch this potential remake at the right time.

Interestingly, though, it does sound like Kitase's priorities lie elsewhere. At the end of the interview, he says that he'd like to spearhead something with a focus on "battle action", but "without losing the characteristics of a Final Fantasy story".

Do you think anything could come of this internal demand for more remakes? Hum the Final Fantasy 6 theme in the comments section below.

Alrighty then, let's get into it. Here's what we're playing on Xbox this weekend:

I think I'm in need of a nice, feel good weekend of gaming. I'd like to play stuff that leaves me feeling all warm and fuzzy. It's appropriate timing, really, considering just how quickly it's getting dark now that the clocks have changed here in the UK.

Top of the agenda is starting The Wolf Among Us Remastered. I claimed the original version with Games with Gold, yet I've still not managed to boot it.
